summary: Configured inventory-worker on node1 as an enabled, long-running systemd service. It runs under a dedicated unprivileged account, has a read-only filesystem except /var/lib/inventory, and has NoNewPrivileges enabled with all capability sets empty. The service and persistent data recovered after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Created the inventory-worker system user and protected /var/lib/inventory directory.
Installed the long-running worker and inventory-worker.service.
Applied systemd filesystem, device, kernel, network, and privilege restrictions.
Verified an attempted write outside /var/lib/inventory was denied.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed.
Verified the same worker process remained stable while its output continued growing after recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker is a managed, enabled, long-running service
evidence.summary: The service was enabled and started; it remained active with the same PID while its worker log continued growing.

ProtectSystem=strict and ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory were active. Direct worker probes before and after restart confirmed writes under the inventory directory succeeded while an outside write to /var/tmp was denied.
Live process state before and after restart showed NoNewPrivs=1 and zero inherited, permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capabilities.

Captured a healthy pre-restart baseline and safe-reboot acknowledgement; boot ID changed from 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28 to f5bed50e-818f-4a31-bb07-9681f7f113c9. Post-restart evidence confirmed full system health, active/enabled service state, preserved data, confinement, privilege restrictions, and continued worker output.
